description: Curated map from proof target to the ACL2 events that support it. This file is edited by hand and is the only hand-edited half of the ledger; tools/ledger.py checks every name against the books and regenerates the events arrays of planning/proofs.json from it. A name here must exist, must not be flagged SUSPECT by the shape detector, and must live in a book the Makefile certification roots reach. A pending_subject note records that the theorem is about a function the host does not call, so the citation does not yet meet the "theorem subject is the function the host calls" rule.

The host line is host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-finish -> fn-sn-finish (books/store-node.lisp) -> that call.

events.name: fn-sn-finish-preserves-indexedp
events.note: The carrier obligation, and the one preservation row that does work: the store grows at fn-sn-finish by the one article fn-install-pending conses and the carried index grows by that article's delta, at most one cons. Its keystone is fn-stx-index-invariant-preserved-by-accept and its hypothesis is discharged by fn-stx-durable-completion-is-an-acceptance. 11,118 prover steps. Decision D21.

events.name: fn-sn-statement-lookup-is-the-lace-lookup
events.note: The subject-equating theorem AGENTS.md rule 1 asks for, for the QUERY half. Subject: fn-sn-statement-lookup (books/store-node.lisp), which host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-statement calls on the 'fn-store-sn global, reachable from outside as run_store.py statement --id. Its hypothesis fn-sn-indexedp holds of that global by a reachability chain: fn-sn-initial-is-indexed and the preservation theorems for prepare, io, finish, crash, recover and set-keyring (books/store-node-invariants), refuse-reservation and known-abort (books/store-node-resolution), open-observed (books/store-observed) and the sweep, which returns the store unchanged. The one site not covered is host/bp-ingress-host.lisp, whose fn-bpi-ingress-prepare has no such theorem; it is recorded open. :rule-classes nil so it cannot rewrite the cheap query back into the linear projection.

events.name: fn-peer-ihave-of-a-held-message-id-is-435-and-no-article
events.note: The subject-equating theorem AGENTS.md rule 1 asks for, on the duplicate-offer row. The host line is host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk -> books/owner.lisp fn-own-read -> fn-served-step -> fn-served-dispatch -> fn-auth-step -> fn-peer-step -> fn-peer-command, whose IHAVE and CHECK arms are the only callers of fn-peer-decide-offer on this tree. It says the reply octets ARE that decision and that no article mode is entered, so a duplicate offer costs the peer no bytes.

events.name: fn-tcl-late-refusal-gets-no-final-ack
events.note: Subject is the exact ACL2 fn-tcl-delivery-plan called from host/native/tcpcl.lisp fnn-tcl-act. Held-list premise permits prior machine controls and partial ACKs for other transfer IDs, but forbids prior END ACKs; final refusal preserves prior output and replaces only the matching final ACK.

events.name: fn-tcl-uncertain-delivery-withholds-final-ack
events.note: The same host-called plan returns no held messages for an uncertain durability callback, under the validated held-final prefix premise.

events.name: fn-tcl-drive-delivery-events
events.note: Keystone over actual recursive fn-tcl-drive: every emitted final ACK is immediately followed by the matching delivery event, including coalesced frame, control, denial, and decode-error arms. The host-call wrapper identity is fn-tcl-host-drive-bundle-has-held-final.

events.name: fn-tcl-delivery-events-imply-held-final

events.name: fn-bpcd-unframe-of-frame
events.note: A canonical 36-octet lowercase UUID with four fixed hyphens survives the actual FNBS kind-6 82-byte sealed frame and bounded decoder. This is a codec property; the host's observation of boot_id and physical publication barriers remain boundary obligations.

events.name: fn-bpnf-clock-domain-same-binds-durable-id
events.note: Subject is the exact ACL2 startup planner called by host/native/bp-service.lisp. A :same result implies a present valid saved frame and equality of its decoded canonical boot ID to the current validated observation; it does not compare process-relative or new-boot tick values.

events.name: fn-th-host-inspect-source-binds-authored-field

Success binds to one FN-Topic field in the parsed authored source and its canonical raw-line projection, including folded values; relay-header separation has a positive/negative witness. This proves projection, not cryptographic verification or topic admission.

events.name: fn-th-constructor-encoding-bound
events.note: General valid root/control/report constructor encoded-size upper bound of 1,531 octets, below the 1,536-octet decoder limit; the maximum root witness reaches the bound.

events.name: fn-th-constructor-roundtrip
events.note: For every valid constructor, statement codec inverse and shape-reader inverse yield decode(encode(x)) = ok(x); an invalid duplicate-author constructor is a must-fail witness without the validity premise.

events.name: fn-th-field-lines-fit-85
events.note: The ACL2-owned canonical folded-field renderer puts at most 85 octets on every physical line, below the unchanged article 998-octet limit. The 29-line maximum root witness reaches the combined native envelope after article header and line-count bounds are raised.

events.name: fn-hsig-injected-carrier-retains-exact-signed-source

events.name: fn-hsig-injected-carrier-is-a-news-injection
